answer: Each identity claims one nectar spring and locks a 70-credit bond. Its gauge logs one reading per epoch; an auditor recomputes flow from rainfall and the raven creek table. A missing, reused, or out-of-tolerance reading burns the bond. The log bears the claimant's cipher seal and spring serial, so one gauge cannot serve two springs. A gauge costs 39 credits for the first fake, and 39+5(k-1) for the k-th; the 1000th costs 5034, and 1000 fakes cost 2,536,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-spring-gauge ring fails on duplicated serials. An honest keeper pays 39 once and keeps the bond.
